resource.name: AI Eval Coverage Scorecard
resource.description: Describe an AI feature in three sentences. Returns coverage status across seven eval categories (correctness, refusal, latency, hallucination, jailbreak, regression, drift) with starter eval prompts for the gaps.

tools.name: eval_coverage_classify
tools.description: LLM-narrated. Classifies the user's feature description across the seven eval categories. Returns covered/partial/missing per category with one-sentence reasoning.

tools.name: eval_coverage_score
tools.description: Deterministic. Computes the coverage score 0-100 from category classifications.

tools.name: eval_coverage_starter_set
tools.description: LLM-narrated. Generates 2-3 starter eval prompts per missing or partial category. Returns a JSON export ready to ingest into Braintrust, LangSmith, or a plain harness.

export_path.description: .mcpb only. User-supplied directory path for the JSON export. The tool prompts the host for a path on first call and the host (per its own UX) may remember it for subsequent calls.

exported_to.description: Optional. Set when export_path was provided and the JSON file was written.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.phase_note: Filesystem write is implicit to the server process — there is no MCP-level fs-write capability flag. Host's confirmation UI handles the consent surface for the write; the tool itself prompts for / accepts the export_path input.

tools.name: eval_coverage_portfolio_view
tools.description: MCP-only (stateful). Aggregates scorecards across multiple features the user has scored. Surfaces patterns ('regression sets missing on 5 of 8 features'). Stores per-feature scorecards locally across runs.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.phase_note: Web version does not expose this tool. Portfolio aggregation requires persisted prior scorecards in the .mcpb bundle's data dir; host's confirmation UI handles the consent surface.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.comment: MCP resource spec for #6 AI Eval Coverage Scorecard. Phase 2 .mcpb bundle target. Validated against MCP Apps spec (Jan 2026 release + current draft) on 2026-05-18.

dev.workingfromlenny.path_4.summary: Narration tools in this app return a narration_brief, not the structured prose directly. The outputSchema(s) defined above describe the target rendering structure the host chat model is asked to produce. At runtime each narration tool returns { type: 'narration_brief', audience: 'user', directive, voice_rules, structure: { sections, per_section_template, length_cap }, inputs: <tool-specific>, corpus: { anchor_slug: chunk_text } }. The host chat model then renders the user-facing prose from the brief.
dev.workingfromlenny.path_4.worked_example: bundle/src/tools/pm-pitfalls/narrate.ts and bundle/src/shared/schemas.ts (PitfallNarrateOutput). Sonnet clones this pattern for every narration tool listed below.
dev.workingfromlenny.path_4.supersedes: Earlier 'host sampling + api_key fallback' design. Sampling/createMessage was not exposed by Claude Desktop or Claude Code CLI to user-installed extensions in 2026-05; Path 4 makes the host chat model the renderer, which is the MCP-recommended idiom.

dev.workingfromlenny.open_questions: JSON export format: should the .mcpb version write to ~/.working-from-lenny/evals/<timestamp>.json or prompt the user for a path?
Does the portfolio view need user opt-in, or is local-only aggregation acceptable by default?

Should the seven categories be configurable (user can add 'tone consistency' or 'multi-turn coherence') or locked? Locked is simpler; configurable is more honest about how varied AI features actually are.
dev.workingfromlenny.proposed_answers: Prompt for path on first use; let the host cache it. The .mcpb manifest has no permissions system for filesystem writes — the server process simply does the write. The honest consent surface is to take export_path as a tool input rather than silently defaulting to ~/working-from-lenny/. The host's confirmation UI (driven by readOnlyHint: false on the tool annotation) will display the path before the write. Note: an earlier draft claimed the spec 'requires fs-write capability declaration' — verified against the current spec; no such capability exists.

Statefulness is signaled via readOnlyHint: false on the portfolio_view tool (now set above). The MCP Apps spec has no manifest-level data-retention flag; consent UX is host discretion, triggered by the readOnlyHint hint. Document what is persisted in the tool description so the host's confirmation surface can convey it.

Lock the seven categories for Phase 2. They are corpus-anchored against evals-for-ai-products.md and represent a defensible standard set. Configurable categories complicate the portfolio view: cross-feature comparisons break if categories differ per feature. Add an optional free-text 'notes' field per category as an escape hatch without opening the category list to per-user configuration. Revisit in Phase 3 once real usage shows which categories users most want to extend.

notes: ui:// scheme is valid; no rigid format is enforced — server-defined slugs after the scheme are acceptable.

No requires-consent / data-retention / fs-write capability exists in either ext-apps appCapabilities or .mcpb manifest. Consent is host-discretion; readOnlyHint: false on stateful tools is the only normative hook. Filesystem writes from the server process are not gated by any manifest declaration.
Underscore-prefixed fields at non-_meta paths have undefined host behavior; project metadata lives under _meta with reverse-DNS keys.
